sample_unit: evaluators (5 physicians, 5 nurses, 5 patients) rating responses to 9 questions from 4 LLMs

links.outcome: Quality, empathy and readability of responses from competing general-purpose vs medical-specific LLMs on the same questions
links.effect: General-purpose models scored higher than medical-specific models across all outcomes; in patients QAMAI 26.0 vs 21.2 (P=0.001), GQS 4.0 vs 2.6 (P=0.007), PETS 75.2 vs 57.6 (P=0.005).
links.quote: General-purpose models consistently scored higher than medical-specific models across all outcomes and evaluator groups.

links.outcome: Readability level of LLM DVT consultation responses using Chinese Readability Platform
links.effect: One medical-specific model required senior high school level; the other three required only junior high school level.
links.quote: Readability varied substantially: one medical-specific model required senior high school level, whereas the other three required only junior high school level.

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates general-purpose versus medical-specific LLMs for perioperative DVT health consultation using physician, nurse, and patient ratings, but does not test a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
